correctness.rationale: For threshold-one three-color CCA and Greenberg–Hastings on K_{a,b}, each site has the same contact palette as its shore peers. The 49 nonempty-palette pair transitions therefore give an exact finite quotient for every a,b>=1. The independently replayed verifier checks all 49 transitions, microscopic periods on 145,440 configurations, 800 exact weighted size/model groups, and each 49-row certificate entry. At a recurrent palette, each local rule bijects the represented colors, so support first-entry equals full-labelled first periodic entry. Full/full palettes yield period three, the recurrent two-palette alternation yields period four, and singleton/singleton yields a fixed point. Cardinality-and-union criteria agree pointwise across models. Exact surjection counts 1, 2^m-2, 3^m-3*2^m+3 prove the displayed full ten-class GHM distribution. Finite quotient exhaustiveness, rather than sampling, is the all-size proof; no arbitrary-graph or general threshold claim is made.

originality.rationale: The earlier recoverable exact biclique CCA census already contains CCA entry and orbit counts, which are explicitly credited. The assessed contribution is a complete ten-class GHM first-entry/period census plus pointwise equality of eventual least periods under genuinely different site updates and unequal transient depths/period-four multiplicities. value.rationale: The central natural question is whether qualitative dynamical similarities of CCA and Greenberg–Hastings persist at the level of individual initial-condition basins on a nontrivial infinite graph family. The exact answer is unexpectedly yes for eventual least period for every same starting state, but no for transient-time distributions and recurrent orbit multiplicities. An exact entire ten-class census, sharp four-update GHM cutoff, and a pointwise rather than aggregate basin identity distinguish substantially more than a routine restatement of the earlier CCA census; the result is useful for comparative excitable-media dynamics and finite biclique test cases.
